correctness.rationale: Every matching count is exact: N_n=sum_j C(3,j)C(n,j)j!=n^3+2n+1, Q_n=N(K_(2,n-1))=n^2-n+1. Odd-intersection matching counts are bounded by |S|Q_n, giving W>=N_n-2|S|Q_n>=2n for odd n and |S|<=(n+1)/2. Even n have odd N_n and thus all multipliers odd. For odd n, the r-star evaluates to 2n, and appending an edge of a second row at a selected column changes the sum by exactly -2n because its conditional signed completion is n. This forces a first zero at r+1 and proves exact minimality. Since r>=2, each of 6r C(n,r) witnesses is uniquely encoded by its r-edge row. Complete exact Walsh enumerations at n=3..7 and independent signed-rook enumeration at n=3..23 corroborate; proof is valid all n>=3.

originality.rationale: The result is an all-width exact first-zero degree for signed matching-count Fourier multipliers in K_(3,n), plus a sharp positive low-degree gap and an explicit family of zeros. The rectangular rook formula supplies only unsigned totals, including the easy even-width parity corollary, while inspected polytope and matching polynomial results make no implication giving the odd-width sharp threshold. Fixed-size and spanning-tree Fourier claims have different quantifiers/configuration families. Indexed equivalence and dominating-parameter queries produced no decisive coverage; residual unindexed priority is acknowledged.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently named signed-rook/monomer-dimer evaluations may already imply the result.
The zero family lower bound is not a complete classification; in n=5 enumeration shows additional first-degree zeros.
The even-width invertibility claim alone is already an immediate classical rook-count parity corollary and is not asserted to be separately novel.

value.rationale: The first vanishing Walsh degree is the exact threshold at which convolution by the matching-incidence indicator loses a low-degree character. Its linear growth with odd graph width, even-odd invertibility distinction, and explicit 6r C(n,r) lost modes quantify an information-recovery boundary for a natural matching model, beyond a textbook total rook count. Neither complete spectral nullity nor all-first-zero classification is claimed.
